I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 135. My first attempt tried to fetch eight source pages at once, and that went over the tool's usage limit. When I tried again with a single page, the tool told me I had no more research calls left for this turn. So I haven't read a single page from your approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages say and give a URL for every point. I won't fill the gap from memory, because those notes would look sourced when they aren't.

**Next step:** Send the request again in a new turn and I'll fetch the sources one or two at a time to stay under the limit. These are the pages I'd planned to read:

- **Verse-by-verse:** enduringword.com (Psalm 135), and Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Barnes on biblehub.com
- **Evangelical:** preceptaustin.org's Psalm 135 page, which often gathers Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* and other older writers
- **Modern scholarship:** netbible.org translator's notes on Psalm 135
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** Augustine's commentary on the Psalms at newadvent.org. He follows the Greek numbering, so this psalm is his Psalm 134.
- **Points where traditions differ:** targeted searches, especially on verse 4 (God choosing Jacob/Israel, where Reformed and Wesleyan views of election may part ways) and verses 15–18 (idols)

If you'd like it done faster, you could also split the job and ask for verses 1–7, then 8–14, then 15–21.
